svg.text: CANopener handheld: DB9 pinout and adapter cables
All cables are CiA 303-1 compatible on CAN A. Wire colours here are for the diagram only.
as you look at the connector on the device
looking into the socket (the cable's plug is the mirror image)
1. OBD-II cable (cars and light trucks; CAN B wired for Ford's body bus, e.g. the F-550)
Other makes put their second bus on other OBD pins (1/9, 12/13 ...): wire that pair to DB9 pins 8 / 4 instead.
OBD pins 2, 10 (J1850) and 15 (L-line) stay unconnected: the handheld has no transceiver for them.
H / J are usually the maker's own second CAN; F / G vary (J1708 or another CAN): check the truck before using them.
Shield: connect at one end only (the handheld's end) to avoid a ground loop.
3. Bench / CANopen cable (CiA 303-1, straight through: CAN A only)
Any off-the-shelf CiA DB9 CAN cable works here. Leave pins 1, 4, 8 unconnected on cables shared with other CiA gear.
A bus with one module on the bench needs termination: the handheld's switch, plus 120 ohm at the far end.
